title: Foundry Local: Cutting-Edge AI experiences on device with ONNX Runtime/Olive — Emma Ning, Microsoft
talk_summary: A Microsoft PM demos Foundry Local, an ONNX Runtime/Olive-based stack for running small language models and MCP-tool agents entirely on-device via a CLI/SDK with hardware-specific model variants. The content is mostly product marketing and a live demo; the only transferable mechanisms are local small-model inference for cheap/private subtasks and a simple 'one model + N MCP servers' agent definition.

takeaways.technique: Local small-model offload for cheap subtasks
takeaways.what_they_do: Run small models (e.g. 1.5B Qwen, Phi-4-mini) on local CPU/GPU via ONNX Runtime instead of cloud, for tasks like summarization and OCR extraction.
takeaways.numbers: ~90 tokens/sec on a 1.5B model on a laptop CPU

takeaways.technique: Hardware-variant model catalog with per-model benchmarking
takeaways.what_they_do: CLI lists each model with variants optimized for CPU/CUDA/iGPU/NPU, and the demo compares two models on quality vs speed before choosing one for the app.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for each model you can get ... different varants optimized for different hardware

takeaways.technique: Minimal agent = one model + N MCP servers
takeaways.what_they_do: An agent is defined declaratively as a single model plus a set of MCP servers; the runtime resolves tools, asks permission per server/directory, then lets the model plan tool calls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: an agent in a foundry local consists of one model and one or more MCP servers

takeaways.technique: Explicit per-resource permission prompts before tool use
takeaways.what_they_do: Before running, the agent asks the user to approve each MCP server and the specific directory it may access.

takeaways.technique: On-device inference to avoid network dependency
takeaways.what_they_do: Runs inference fully locally so demos/apps work offline and without cloud round-trips.
takeaways.evidence_quote: my lab demo runs entirely locally
